subject: StreamlineAI — competitive snapshot + token-econ next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: StreamlineAI — competitive snapshot + token-econ next steps

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned:

What we covered (high level)
- Redwood strengths: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, batching + KV caching primitives, predictable dedicated throughput with SLA, and tooling for unit economics (batching/cache knobs exposed).
- Demo highlights: streaming latency with 64-token window, example cache hit that cut downstream token cost.

Ask / next tests we propose:
1) A 1M-token economics run using your production prompt mix (we attach a cost-model CSV to baseline assumptions).
2) Batch-shape sensitivity: run three profiles (optimistic: large batches tail-heavy, realistic: mixed, conservative: small batches).
3) Cache-hit scenarios: 0%, 30%, 70% — measure token reduction, end-to-end P95 latency, and CPU/GPU utilization.
4) Latency SLO check at your target QPS (you mentioned 50k concurrent users, avg 25 tokens/req) — confirm P95 under peak bursts.

I've attached the deck and a starter cost model (streamline-cost-model.csv). Can you confirm the prompt distribution and whether the data needs to stay inside your VPC? That will determine whether we propose Hosted, Dedicated, or Private for the PoC.

Planned owners: Vanessa will draft the test matrix; Rishi will run the harness if we have sample prompts/traffic. I'll put together a short TCO one-pager for execs.

Next steps:
- Samir/Elena: share prompt sample + any network/egress constraints by EOD Thu (11/04).
- Redwood: produce baseline 1M-token TCO and a short competitive note vs the hyperscaler you mentioned.

Attachments: streamline-demo-slides.pdf, streamline-cost-model.csv

Thanks — happy to hop back on a quick call to triage assumptions.

Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Khan <samir@streamline.ai>

Subject: Re: StreamlineAI — competitive snapshot + token-econ next steps

Ben — appreciate the recap and the deck. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Competitive asks: can you provide an apples-to-apples per-1M-token comparison vs HyperscalerX (their managed inference) and InferenceAPIY? The execs want a simple table showing hosted list price, typical dedup/overhead, and expected floor with caching/batching.

2) For the 1M-token run, use our chat workload profile: ~25 tokens/req average, 2.8 messages/session, bursty traffic peaks (we see 4x baseline during promos). We expect ~50k concurrent users during peak.

3) Cache assumptions: we currently target 70% prefix reuse on user histories; can you show results for 0/30/70/90% cache hit? Also include network egress assumptions — approx 45TB/month to EU customers if that matters.

4) Security: we need SOC2 + brief on key management and VPC connectivity for the PoC. Procurement will need docs.

If you can produce a one-page TCO (simple numbers) and a recommended PoC scope for a two-week trial, that would help fast-track procurement review.

Thanks,
Samir

samir@streamline.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-11-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: StreamlineAI — competitive snapshot + token-econ next steps

Samir / Elena — thanks, quick initial snapshot and a proposed experiment plan. Rishi and I will refine once we get the prompt sample.

Initial competitive snapshot (hosted / production assumptions)
- Redwood (hosted): baseline ~ $18 / 1M tokens (includes streaming overhead, batching baseline).
- Redwood (dedicated, optimized with batching + 70% cache): equivalent marginal cost ~ $8–10 / 1M tokens at sustained throughput (depends on token length distribution and batching shapes).
- HyperscalerX (managed inference): list price often looks like $12 / 1M for inference-only but does not include orchestration, idle reserved capacity, or KV cache savings — effective floor closer to $10–14 depending on your autoscaling/idle penalties.
- InferenceAPIY: shorter tail on latency but higher per-token egress and less aggressive KV caching — floor ~$14–$20 / 1M under realistic loads.

Key differentiators to highlight in PoC:
- Transparent per-route cost breakdown and token-level traces (helps debug tail costs).
- Built-in prefix/KV caching that reduces token bill when history reuse is high.
- Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and reduced autoscale cold-starts.

Proposed quick experiment matrix (we recommend Redwood run these in our PoC environment):
A) 1M-token baseline run with your prompt mix (measure token counts, P50/P95 latency, GPU utilization).
B) Batch-shape sweep: small (avg batch 4), medium (20), large (100) — measure throughput per-GPU and P95 latency.
C) Cache hit sweep: 0%, 30%, 70%, 90% — report net token billing delta and latency changes.
D) Failover/fallback exercise: simulate 20% model variant fallback and measure service continuity and cost delta.

Rishi will own the harness. Ben will send the TCO one-pager. I attached a short plain-text compare for quick read (redwood-quick-compare.txt).

Timeline suggestion:
- Thu 11/04: Streamline sends sample prompts + egress constraints.
- Fri 11/05: Redwood provides one-page TCO and updated cost CSV.
- Mon 11/08–Fri 11/12: Two-week PoC window (we can start microbenchmarks immediately).

If that works, Rishi and I will spin up the test harness and send a detailed runbook.

Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
